readingInstruction: Read Psalm 118:19-29. This is the climax of the Hallel, the psalms sung at Passover. Jesus quoted verses 22 and 23 about himself in Mark 12, and the crowds shouted verse 26 on Palm Sunday. Read it as the song of the King entering the gate.
settingTheScene: Psalm 118 is a song of thanksgiving for victory, probably sung in a procession to the temple. The singer has been surrounded by enemies and has been saved by the LORD. Now he comes to the gates of the temple to give thanks. The last stanza, our reading, is full of lines that the New Testament applies to Jesus: the gate, the rejected stone, the day the LORD has made, and the blessed one who comes in the LORD’s name.
observation: “Open to me the gates of righteousness, that I may enter through them and give thanks to the LORD” (v. 19).
“I thank you that you have answered me and have become my salvation” (v. 21).
“The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone” (v. 22).
“This is the LORD’s doing; it is marvelous in our eyes” (v. 23).
“This is the day that the LORD has made; let us rejoice and be glad in it” (v. 24).
“Save us, we pray, O LORD! O LORD, we pray, give us success!” (v. 25).
“Blessed is he who comes in the name of the LORD! We bless you from the house of the LORD” (v. 26).
“Oh give thanks to the LORD, for he is good; for his steadfast love endures forever!” (v. 29).
interpretation:
The singer approaches the gates of the temple and asks them to open. “This is the gate of the LORD; the righteous shall enter through it.” Only the righteous may enter the presence of God, and the question of who is righteous is raised. The answer will come in Christ. He is the righteous one who enters, and through him we enter.

The singer thanks God for answering and becoming his salvation. The word for salvation is yeshuah, the root of the name Jesus. Then comes the famous line: “The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.” The builders, perhaps the nations or the leaders, threw away a stone as unfit, and it was exactly the stone that held the building together. Israel, small and despised, was chosen by God. David, the youngest son, was passed over and made king. Above all, Jesus was rejected by the leaders of his people and made the cornerstone of the new temple, the church. He applied this verse to himself in the parable of the tenants (Mark 12:10-11), and Peter applied it in Acts 4:11. “This is the LORD’s doing; it is marvelous in our eyes.” The resurrection and exaltation of the rejected Christ is God’s doing.

“This is the day that the LORD has made; let us rejoice and be glad in it.” Christians have long sung this verse on Easter, the day the LORD made in a special way.

“Save us, we pray, O LORD!” In Hebrew, this is hoshia na, which became “Hosanna.” When the crowd shouted “Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!” on the road to Jerusalem, they were quoting this psalm and treating Jesus as the long-awaited one. Verse 26 declares a blessing on the one who comes, and also on the pilgrims. The psalm calls for a festal procession with branches up to the horns of the altar, the same image as the palms on the road.

The psalm closes where it began: “Oh give thanks to the LORD, for he is good; for his steadfast love endures forever!” Jesus and his disciples most likely sang this psalm at the end of the Last Supper, shortly before he went to be rejected. The song he sang about the rejected stone was about himself.
connection: Isaiah 28:16 speaks of the tested cornerstone laid in Zion. Matthew 21:42, Mark 12:10-11, and Luke 20:17 record Jesus quoting verse 22. Acts 4:11, Ephesians 2:20-22, and 1 Peter 2:4-8 apply the stone to Christ. Matthew 21:9 and John 12:13 have the crowd quoting verse 26. Matthew 26:30 says they sang a hymn after the Supper. Romans 9:33 and 10:11 speak of the stone and those who believe in him. Revelation 21:22 says the Lamb is the temple.
application:
Pray “This is the day the LORD has made” as you start tomorrow. Choose to rejoice.

Think of a time when something rejected became a blessing in your life. Thank God for it.

Say “Hosanna” today, “Save us, we pray.” Name what needs saving.
prayerPrompts: Ask God to open the gates of righteousness for you.
Thank Jesus, the stone the builders rejected.
Thank him that this is the day the LORD has made.
